backlog.item: Training with carried state between a user’s windows
backlog.why: Moved up 10-18 (user): full-history context at short-window speed (2,048 windows ~5x faster than 32k). Designed, CPU prototype exact; code started 10-18

backlog.item: Instant-weighted (x2) final decay (fixed and checked, ready to run)
backlog.why: Moved back 10-18: instant already passes the bar (+0.94%) and the weighting likely costs curve, the failing head. Insurance if a later model slips on instant

backlog.item: Teacher targets from the fork’s full-history replay
backlog.why: Needed with carried state; 5.2 h GPU, 3.7 GB

backlog.item: State compression trained in (QAT) at ~400/400 bits per card/note, during the final decay only
backlog.why: Post-training test: 60× smaller state than int8 for +0.0012 / +0.0023 nats. Redo only the final decay from epoch 10 with the compression in the loop. Sped up: fused GPU kernel, no eigensolver (same codec, bitwise on real states); CPU projection 75–80 min. A 10-min GPU benchmark decides the launch

backlog.item: Muon optimizer for the student
backlog.why: Outside pointer: largest instant gains (−0.0005 instant at d=32); our student is AdamW only

backlog.item: Label-free reference: the fork fine-tuned with review type switched off
backlog.why: Honest best a big model can do without review type. Fine-tune first: a cheap from-scratch fork-size retrain lost +0.0037 / +0.0043 in outside runs

backlog.item: Deployment-realistic scoring without the duration leak
backlog.why: Intervals as Anki knows them when it shows the card; both models, cheap. Outside runs: +0.0002 / +0.0004 cost

backlog.item: Exact kernel work for the w64 width
backlog.why: w64 still ~21% slower than the w32 fast kernels at short windows; bit-for-bit identical

backlog.item: More parallel windows at long lengths (8,192 × 8)
backlog.why: Timing test first, then a learning-rate check

backlog.item: Real-timestamp inputs (card age, time since any review, creation batch)
backlog.why: Outside pointer: about −0.0005 / −0.0008 net of the clock leak; needs the dataset build with timestamps

backlog.item: Long-history summary inputs for short windows
backlog.why: Card prior reviews, FSRS state, user pass rate; modest prior

backlog.item: Robustness to other apps: pass/fail-only ratings, no durations
backlog.why: Same test as the review-type one, CPU

backlog.item: Grade-order sanity: interval(Again) ≤ Hard ≤ Good ≤ Easy
backlog.why: Measure how often the student breaks it; enforcing it cost +0.002 on curve in outside runs

backlog.item: Open tuning queue from outside research (Muon learning rate x0.5 / x2, longer warmup)
backlog.why: Pointers only: we keep our own training setup (decision 10-17)

results.name: 732-user readout (new standard set): 32k dec10 vs carried state v2 / v1 / no carry
results.takeaway: Same order as on 464 users. dec10 is 0.03 pp from the curve bar on this set; v2 vs dec10 +0.00028 [+0.00003, +0.00054] / +0.00042 [+0.00036, +0.00048]
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx32768c-dec10/w8+s8 (732 pool)

results.name: Carried state v2 (strided lanes, exact state): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay at 2,048, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Best 2,048-window model by far: −0.0009 / −0.0013 vs no carry, −0.0009 / −0.0011 vs v1. Before decay it beats 32k e10 (−0.0002 / −0.0011); after decay it trails 32k dec10 by +0.0003 [−0.0001, +0.0007] / +0.0004: the 2,048 decay gains less than the 32k one. Next: decay v2 at 32k
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-sc-lanes-dec12/w8+s8

results.name: Carried state v1, arm B (control, no carry): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Gate users at e12: carry beat it by −0.0013 / −0.0005 (CIs below zero); on 464 users after decay only the instant gain holds (−0.0002)
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-sc-zero-dec12/w8+s8

results.name: Carried state v1, arm A (carry): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Paired with arm B (same recipe, no carry), 464 users: −0.00001 / −0.00020 after decay [curve CI −0.0003, +0.0003; instant −0.00033, −0.00007]; before decay (e12) −0.00056 / −0.00041. The decay erased most of the curve gain. Both 2,048-window arms stay behind 32k (+0.0012 / +0.0015). v2 (exact state) is running
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-sc-carry-dec12/w8+s8

results.name: After-training compression of dec10 with codebooks fitted on dec10’s own states
results.takeaway: Same cost as the codebooks from the earlier model (+0.00127 / +0.00231 vs +0.00120 / +0.00231). The cost is the bit budget, not the codebook fit
results.label: dec10/w8+vq378x412 (dec10 books)

results.name: State compression (~400/400 bits per card/note) trained into the final decay, scored compressed
results.fork: fork 0.32132 / 0.28497 on the same users; compressed after training (dec10) 0.32314 / 0.28946; uncompressed dec10 0.32194 / 0.28716
results.takeaway: Worse than compressing after training (+0.0012 / +0.0010). Not a codec mismatch, not stale codebooks (refitting them on the new model’s states: 0.32799 / 0.29382, worse still; it learned around the frozen books). Training with the compression in the loop hurts here; dropped for now
results.label: qat/w8+vq378x412

results.name: Review-number flags as inputs (2nd / 3rd / 4th+ review), 2 epochs at 2,048 + decay
results.takeaway: No gain: curve +0.00003 [−0.00005, +0.00012], instant −0.00004 [−0.00006, −0.00003] (233 / 256 of 464 users better). Instant gain real but ~1/10 of what would matter. Dropped; at 32k the model can count reviews itself anyway
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx2048crf-dec8

results.name: Calibration fitted offline on the dec10 student (temperature + bias, user-split cross-validation)
results.fork: fork 0.29766 / 0.27216 (calibrated the same way: 0.29761 / 0.27214); uncalibrated student 0.30096 / 0.27471
results.takeaway: Nothing to fold into the export: both models are equally (and barely) miscalibrated, gains are ~5e-5. Spaced slice unchanged: +0.79% / +0.84%.
results.label: sm12-calib

results.name: One-epoch final decay at 2,048 windows (vs our quarter epoch)
results.fork: fork 0.29766 / 0.27216; same start with a quarter-epoch decay 0.30259 / 0.27668
results.takeaway: Longer decay helps: −0.00033 curve [−0.00068, −0.00008] / −0.00019 instant [−0.00025, −0.00012] (292 / 351 of 464 users better). Smaller than the gain seen in outside runs; a 1-epoch decay at 32k would cost ~4½ h
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx2048c-dec8-1ep/w8+s8

results.name: Speed check of the compression-in-training GPU kernels
results.fork: seconds per update: plain 1.12, with compression 1.38 (fused kernels), 3.4–3.8 (PyTorch loop)
results.takeaway: Worse than compressing after training (+0.0012 / +0.0010). Not a codec mismatch, not stale codebooks (refitting them on the new model’s states: 0.32799 / 0.29382, worse still; it learned around the frozen books). Training with the compression in the loop hurts here; dropped for now

results.name: Training speed profile (quiet GPU): student at 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 windows and the fork-size model
results.takeaway: Long windows cost the student a lot (5× slower at 32k than at 2,048). The fork-size model at batch 128 trains faster than the student at 16k+ windows, so a label-free fork-size reference is affordable
